title: Static S-Curved Snake
description: One original stylised limbless snake-inspired animal, with a broad slightly raised flattened head, narrowed neck, one long variable-thickness body following two opposite S bends and a fine tapering tail. Head, neck, body and tail are one continuous closed shared-vertex mesh; two small dark lateral eyes and one small thick forked tongue are separately editable complete meshes with visible seated roots. The tongue has an actual open V notch between its two tips, not a painted line. A pale belly is assigned to the lower faces of the same full body, with finite flat ground facets; it is not a second overlapping skin. All whole-path coordinates, section proportions, head, taper and tongue outline are newly authored. Not the old mooring rope given eyes, an octopus arm extracted, a snail without its shell, or a stretched tadpole. Only generic mesh orientation, ear clipping, eye primitive and mature export/render tools are reused. Four closed meshes, four opaque matte untextured PBR materials. Metres, native Z up, head/front -Y, full horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One prop, zero scenes or extra poses. Artistic fixed exterior only: no real species, scale-row pattern, internal skeleton, biological anatomy, venom or dangerousness identification, mouth motion, sensing, locomotion, slithering simulation, rig, animation, collision, welfare or ecological performance claim.
